tasks.title: The panel's supply model is wrong in three ways
tasks.needs: Decide: fix the scr_curve formula, or keep the panel as a rough read-out and treat gm balance as the authority? The tool prints both numbers side by side, so this is a preference rather than a discovery.
tasks.notes: scr_curve_report computes available = min(money/price, slots) x best dps. (1) It prices EVERYTHING at the tower with the best dps per dollar - Pina Collider at $100 - so on waves 1-11, where the purse is $30-$93, it buys ZERO towers and prints "?" while the player has a board full of $5 towers. (2) It uses damage x rate x targets with targets = 10, which assumes ten monsters are inside a 75px range at once; they spawn 0.5s apart and walk ~1.26px a step, so they sit ~37px apart over an 1840px route - two or three, not ten. (3) It credits a tower with its full dps along the WHOLE route, when it fires only while a monster is inside its range: on 1-1 that is 9%-15% of the route. Together the three make the panel optimistic by roughly an order of magnitude, which is why it read ok while the play leaked. DECIDED (status quo): the in-game panel stays a ROUGH read-out and `gm balance` stays the authority.  The panel's kinder supply model is not being fixed, and the two numbers it and the tester print side by side are the intended way to see the gap. Closed on rayu's instruction 2026-10-14 ('the rest are good').

tasks.title: The headless sim (P2): leaks, hearts and real target caps
tasks.notes: P1 is the closed form: it answers "can this income field enough coverage to meet a wave's demand", which is a ratio. It cannot say how many leak or how many hearts are left, and those are what the feel targets should be written against. The sim time-steps the real rules: monsters spawn one per 0.5s rather than as a burst, towers fire with their own targets cap, kills pay money as they land (so wave 10 cannot be bought at wave 1), and a leak costs a life and pays nothing. Deliverables: leaks per wave, hearts left, idle money, and the delivered-vs-nominal dps gap.

tasks.title: The sim needs a HUMAN spending policy, not a wave-boundary greedy
tasks.notes: `gm balance sim --spend ceiling` re-runs the greedy at each wave boundary, which is perfect play with perfect information - and money that sits idle for 20s is towers the player did not have DURING the wave, so it is optimistic in the same direction the panel was. Two measured reasons it matters: the run leaves $12 unspent at the end while only ever buying $5 Daisies after wave 1 (the purse arrives in $5-8 chunks and the greedy will not save), and the greedy CONCENTRATES - all 20 towers land in two blocks on the route because it takes the highest-coverage cell first and ties go in map order, so the last 40% of the route is bare. Deliverables: `--spend instant` (buy the moment money allows, mid-wave), a tie-break that spreads along the route, rungs as a competitor (needs the policy to remember a level across waves), and an idle-money figure per wave so "the income cannot be spent" is measurable rather than inferred. The ceiling stays: it is the upper bound the fit compares against.  ORDERING 2026-10-14 (plan "Make the numbers true"): `balance-fit-from-sim` cannot start until this lands - a fit against a perfect-play spender is a fit against a player who does not exist (LL-038). This is WP2 of the plan and needs no decision from rayu, so it is the next thing to build.  DONE 2026-10-15, and the measurement was worse than the card assumed. Three deliverables, all landed: (1) --spend instant re-runs the greedy every 15 frames while a wave is LIVE, so a kill to become a tower inside the wave that earned it - the run now ends holding $2 instead of $17; (2) the route-spreading tie-break became a change of OBJECTIVE, not a tie-break: coverage was ADDITIVE and double-counted, so two towers over one stretch both scored it - $300 bought 15 towers shooting 41% of a 1841px route with the last quartile at 0%. Scoring UNION coverage (submodular, so the density greedy keeps its 1-1/e bound) covers 100% of the route with 14 towers, and on the same $143 the sim goes from 16 towers / 33% wasted swings / widest in-range list 6 to 11 / 25% / 3; (3) rungs are now a competitor across waves because the policy is handed the towers STANDING - it was told only which CELLS were taken, so a rung was invisible every wave. The instant run builds 9 upgraded towers instead of 11 cheap ones. Idle money is recorded per wave (idle and money_end on WaveResult) and printed by the report. Written up as LL-048. Consequence: the 10-target finding got STRONGER (6 to 3) and its test now says why instead of just moving.

tasks.title: Decide the upgrade tween vs the placed size
tasks.notes: A tower is PLACED at draw_scale 0.5, but the purchase tween is tower_selection.draw_scale = lerp(0.25, 0.70, _frac) with _frac = level/10 and a cap of 5 (objects/_levelControl/Step_0.gml line 180). So the first upgrade takes a tower to about 0.34, and even the cap only reaches 0.475 - upgrading makes a tower SMALLER and it never gets back to the size it was placed at. Either normalise the tween to the cap of 5 (0.25 .. 0.70 across levels 1-5), or bring the placed size down to match the ladder. (was fix-tower-upgrade-scale)  STILL TRUE 2026-10-14, and the ladder moved under it: tower_cap() is 5 + mastery with tower_floor() = cap - 4, so `_frac = level/10` spans 0.10-0.50 at zero mastery (draw_scale 0.295-0.475 - never reaching the 0.5 it was placed at) and only 0.52 at the first mastery node. Step_0.gml line 180 still reads lerp(0.25,0.70,_frac). ANSWERED 2026-10-14: neither of the two options this card offered. The card asked whether to normalise the tween to the cap (0.25..0.70 across levels 1-5) or to bring the placed size down to match the ladder. Both keep a size cue that has to be re-derived every time the ladder moves - and both leave the original complaint in place, that an upgrade is the one purchase in the game that makes the thing you bought LOOK SMALLER (a placed 0.5 becomes 0.34 at L2 and does not regain 0.5 until L10). DECISION: the size stops carrying the level. draw_scale is frozen at the placed 0.5 and the level is carried by an outline colour - level 1 has none, levels 2-10 each get their own - which is legible at any level, costs no new art, and cannot be made wrong by a ladder change. See tower-level-look (the wiring) and tower-level-palette (the colours).

tasks.title: The damage pipeline takes its amount as an argument

PROOF: gm balance project --all-waves and gm balance sim captured before and after are byte-identical (diff says so), which is the only honest evidence a no-op refactor was one. tasks.title: Depth: sort plants, monsters and gravestones by the feet, every step
tasks.notes: DIAGNOSIS (LL-059): there was no sorting at all - three formulas. Monsters were a flat depth = -60 written in three places; plants were -60 - (y>>5) at placement, which is ALWAYS more negative, so a plant drew in front of every monster wherever either stood; the six gravestones were -(y/room_height)-50, one flat value for all six in an 800px room. FIX: one function, scr_depth_y(y) in scripts/scr_setDepth (which held a dead GM8 scr_setDepth whose sign was backwards), depth = -60 - y/32 on the band plants already used, plus a 1e-5 id tie-break so two monsters queueing on the same path pixel cannot flicker. Monsters re-derive it in obj_mon/Step_0 EVERY step (all states) and once in Create from the spawn point; plants and gravestones derive it at creation, the grave from y-16 because that is where its art is drawn. scr_depth_band() is the same arithmetic without id, for the DEPTH boot log line - a diagnostic that cannot throw (LL-002). The old literals in scr_zombie_emerge and scr_zombie_path are gone, so there is exactly one writer of an actor depth.  VALIDATED BY rayu 2026-10-19: plants, monsters and gravestones sort by the feet, every step. The DEPTH boot line and the crossover timing agree with what is on screen.  TIE-BREAK 2026-10-19: the per-instance buffer is `irandom(97) * 0.00001`, rolled once, not `id mod 97`. GameMaker re-saved the script from its own buffer at 17:27 with the project open and that save carried the other line; the behaviour is identical (stable, at most 0.00097 of a depth unit), the comment and the test now describe what is on disk, and the card stays validated. Written up as LL-063, with the rule that a test asserts the PROPERTY, not the line.

tasks.title: hp and money columns diverge once the curve is raised
tasks.notes: The difficulty columns scale hp by 1.0/1.5/2.5 but money by only 1.0/1.25/1.5. That mismatch is invisible at curve_end 13 and tears at 28: measured, Brutal/Normal goes from 0.93/0.57 = 1.63 today to 1.89/0.58 = 3.26 with the compressed prices. So "recalculate so the difficulties map the same way" cannot be done by moving curve_end alone - the money column has to be re-derived with it (Brutal money wants to be about 2.5 to match its hp, which is on-theme: Brutal is documented as the way a skilled player accelerates tower collection).  MEASURED 2026-10-13 by `gm balance sim` (LL-042): the divergence is not a property of a raised curve_end - it is LIVE AT curve_end 13, and it is an artefact of the rounding. `scr_zomb_death` pays round(kill_money x money_mult) and the common Grumble-Mulch pays 1, so Hard's x1.25 rounds back to 1 (a no-op) while Brutal's x1.50 rounds to 2 (a doubling). Income over stage 1-1 is $122 / $128 / $247 against hp multipliers of 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.5, so hp per dollar is 1.00 / 1.17 / 1.01 - HARD is the hardest difficulty and Brutal the easiest. The sim shows it as an outcome, not a ratio: Brutal clears 1-1 with 20 hearts and $22 spare, Hard leaks 19 and survives on one, and Hard FAILS on fast ground (z=2). So "Brutal money wants to be about 2.5" is not the whole fix: no multiplier below 1.5 can be told apart from Normal. Options: accumulate money fractionally and round only for display, raise the base kill payout so the column scales a large number, or move the rounding to the payout site. A design call, and it belongs WITH the price change rather than before it.

tasks.title: scr_zombie_emerge resets life to maxLife - every shot at an emerging monster is erased
tasks.notes: scr_level_spawn calls scr_level_difficulty() at instance_create, so a monster has its FULL life before the 60-step emerge - which means it is targetable from the spawn point. But scr_zombie_emerge ends with data[MON.life] = data[MON.maxLife], so every point of damage dealt during the emerge is silently undone; and scr_zomb_death is only reached from scr_zombie_path, so a monster sitting at 0 hp during the emerge survives to start walking. Net effect: a tower covering the spawn spends about a second of fire per monster into a life reset, and because the emerging monster is the NEAREST instance it is that tower's PREFERRED target. Two things to settle: was the reset meant to make the emerge untargetable (then the monster should not be findable - find_all_range should skip it), or should the damage persist (then drop the reset)? Either way it makes tower placement a real decision, so the sim has to model it rather than assume it away.  DECIDED 2026-10-18: DAMAGE PERSISTS. The reset is deleted (scr_zombie_emerge now only calls scr_changeState at step 60), so the card's two options resolved to the second one. Why not "make the emerge untargetable" instead: a monster that is not shootable is a monster the player cannot learn to pre-fire, and hiding it from find_all_range would have made tower placement LESS decisive, not more. A monster killed during the emerge now walks for one frame and dies on the first path frame, because scr_zomb_death still runs from scr_zombie_path - that one-frame delay is the only visible trace, and it is why the HP bar can show 0 through the last emerge frame.

tasks.title: The tower click mask must not scale with the art
tasks.notes: obj_tower already carried spr_tower_click_region in its .yy - the mask was never wrong. It arrived at 16x32 because obj_tower/Create_0 drew the art with image_xscale = image_yscale = 0.5, and a collision mask SCALES with image_xscale: mask_index does not exempt an instance from that. The art's size therefore moved into draw_scale (0.5 placed, 0.25 for the ghost), image_xscale / image_yscale are now +/-1 FACING ONLY, and drawing goes through the new scr_draw_self_scaled(). Every consumer of the size followed: scr_drawLight (the shadow silhouette), scr_drawGlowOutline (the hover halo), draw_self_part (the in-water part draw, which gained optional _sx/_sy so its existing callers behave identically) and the upgrade tween in _levelControl/Step_0, which now writes draw_scale and so can no longer un-mirror a tower (LL-012). The step-1 click box is gone: Step_1 asks the mask itself with position_meeting(mouse_x, mouse_y, id), and _levelControl picks the tower whose OWN cell holds the pointer when two stacked towers are both under it. THE SAME MASK was then making the placement ghost lie: obj_tower_edit/Step_0 asked position_meeting(x,y,obj_tower) for occupancy, which reads the 32x64 mask, so the cell above a tower went red even though obj_tower/Create_0 blocks one cell and two towers may stack. That test is now mp_grid_get_cell on LEVEL.path_grid - the grid the tower will be written into - plus a _spawn test, and a refusal logs META [PATH] placement refused: <why> instead of refusing silently. No .yy edits were needed. Written up as LL-033. REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED 2026-10-12: rayu hit `ERROR ... of Draw Event for object obj_mon: undefined value at gml_Script_draw_self_part (line 33) - _x = x - sprite_get_xoffset(sprite_index)*_sx`, every frame a monster was in water. Not the mask this time - the OPTIONAL _sx/_sy arguments this card added. draw_self_part DECLARES seven parameters (argument0..argument6) but obj_mon/Draw_0 passes five, and the argument list is sized to the DECLARED arity (unpassed parameters padded with undefined), so the old test `(argument_count > 5) ? argument5 : image_xscale` took the argument5 branch and multiplied by undefined. Proof it was the count and not image_xscale: the error says 'undefined value', not 'not set before reading it', so the slot exists and holds undefined; obj_mon never assigns image_xscale anything but a real; and scr_meta_log declares ONE parameter while printing TEN, so argument_count = max(declared, passed) fits both. Every other argument_count user in the project declares ZERO parameters, which is why only this call broke. The test is now is_undefined(argument5)/is_undefined(argument6) - the project's usual 'not there' question, independent of how argument_count is computed - and scr_drawGlowOutline (same brittle shape, argument_count > 0) was fixed with it. Written up as LL-035.

tasks.title: Towers mirror to face their target

The helper accepts every shape target takes - an instance from instance_nearest, an array from find_all_range, noone, or the -1 find_all_range returns when nothing is found - faces the NEAREST valid target, holds the last facing when there is nothing to face, and ignores a target inside a 2px dead zone so a monster in the cell directly above or below cannot strobe the sprite. Written up as an extension of LL-012.

tasks.title: A wave ends only when every zombie is killed or reaches the exit
tasks.notes: With no towers the zombies vanished a few seconds into every wave: the anti-softlock valve in scr_level_wait fired on elapsed time (6 s after the wave finished spawning) and deleted EVERY live monster. A stopwatch cannot tell slow from stuck, and a zombie needs 20-45 s to walk a stage at about 0.75 px/step, so the valve was really the end of every wave: the zombies never reached the despawn, lose_life() never ran, no life was ever paid, level_leaked stayed 0, Untouched was still earned and the stage still cleared. The leak then life then game over mechanic was being discarded silently, and the leak path printed nothing at all. The valve now fires on evidence about the monster: scr_zomb_updatePosition counts steps in which path_position does not change (the path follower own report, which - unlike x/y - cannot be fooled by an instance that has lost its path and is drifting, LL-025), and scr_level_wait clears only the monster that has not advanced for 5 s, logging path_free and path_retry, with level_forced set. Five seconds sits above the ~2 s obj_mon/Alarm_0 needs to escalate to the tower-ignoring escape grid, and a ten-minute per-wave latch (>= plus a flag, never ==, LL-029) keeps roadmap 4.4.1 promise that a stage can never hang. Every fate is now labelled once in the log - kill / leak / valve - plus one line per monster with path length, px/step and the projected walk time, so any future threshold is derived from the log rather than guessed. Written up as LL-031 and in systems_overview 4.3.1.

DRAWN IN Draw_73, which is the level's Post Draw AND already the grid's own layer: it brightens bck_drawGrid additively at 0.5 while a tower is being placed, so the highlight is the grid brightening rather than a second thing laid over it.  That layer draws OVER every instance, which is why the square tints the plant's lower pixels too; drawing it under the art instead is not an event swap but a DEPTH question (it must be over the ground and under the towers), so it is left as a look decision rather than guessed.  ONE place answers 'which tower is the pointer over': Step_0 sets tower_hovered exactly where the hover is decided, and the flag it already set for the tower's own Draw is read from the same line - so the cell, the level and the glow cannot name different towers.  The LEVEL is drawn with bm_normal, because a black outline adds NOTHING under additive blending and the number would come out as bare white (LL-046).  Its height comes from the sprite's bbox top MINUS its origin, which is LL-047: sprite_get_bbox_top() is measured from the sprite CANVAS, not the origin, and every tower sprite puts its origin at the plant's feet (spr_t3_idle: bbox_top 3, yorigin 75, so -72 - the first version printed the number across the stem).  Guarded end to end because a draw path must not throw (LL-002): a control object that outlived its level, or a tower that exists but has not been handed its data yet, draws nothing at all.  CHANGED THE SAME DAY, after the first look at it (2026-10-15): the cell was HALVED - _fill 0.20 -> 0.10, _edge 0.45 -> 0.25 - because it was competing with the new ring for the same attention.  The spr_towerRange decal was RETIRED: it filled the whole circle with a soft wash at 15% and was driven by tower_selection, so a CLICK covered a large part of the garden and the ground under it stopped being readable.  In its place the range is a 3px additive white RING at tower_range_alpha (0.25, raised from 0.15), drawn for the HOVERED tower - three draw_circle calls, because draw_circle draws a 1px outline and takes no width argument, and it is the same call the placement circle already uses (obj_tower_edit/Draw_0).  The ring reads the same _hov as the cell and the level, so all three cannot name different towers (LL-021); the guard above them now tests max(TOWER.level, TOWER.range) - the LAST field the block reaches for - so reordering the enum cannot turn a guard into a crash.  ONE EXCEPTION KEPT ON PURPOSE: while the pointer is over the card's range band, the SELECTED tower is ringed, because the band exists to name a tower's reach and would otherwise promise something it no longer delivers.  NOTE FOR THE OWNER: spr_towerRange is now referenced by nothing but the project's resource list - it has not been deleted, so the decal can be brought back, and it can be retired with it if you prefer; that decision is not worth a card of its own.

tasks.title: The HUD wave counter is one ahead of wave_count
tasks.notes: STATINV.waves starts at 1 while wave_count starts at 0, so the display reads one high and scr_zomb_pathSpeed computes speed for the wrong wave. REFS CORRECTED 2026-10-14: `wave_count = 0` now lives in scr_setupSpawning (line 41) and the `waves` static item is created in scr_setup_statinv (line 32) - _levelControl/Create_0 no longer mentions either name, so the old ref pointed at a file that cannot answer the question. scr_level_spawn still does `wave_count++` and `add_item_value(waves,1)` together (lines 17-18), so the off-by-one is unchanged and still carried: the sim models it as `stat_waves(wave) = wave + 1` and test_balance asserts exactly that. DONE 2026-10-14 (WP1a, LL-044). The fix is TWO edits, not one, because the item had two consumers: `_levelControl/Create_0.gml` now seeds `waves` at 0 (so it equals `wave_count`, and the HUD number, the level log and the scr_zomb_pathSpeed ramp are all right), and `scr_level_showPath.gml` - the one reader that wants the NEXT wave - asks for `get_item_value(waves) + 1` itself. On the Python side `Sim.stat_waves` was `return wave + 1`, restating the bug; it now reads the seed out of the GML (`constants.wave_seed`, read by tables.py) and returns `seed + wave`, so a revert moves the sim with the game. tasks.title: Revive shd_outline: an explicit colour uniform, drawn at draw_scale
tasks.notes: A REVIVAL, not a new shader. shd_outline is a registered GMShader and scr_getOutlineShd() and scr_drawSelfOutlined() both exist - and NOTHING CALLS EITHER SCRIPT. It is ported dead code, the same class as the reflections in LL-043. Two reasons it cannot be used as it stands. (1) scr_drawSelfOutlined ends in draw_self(), which draws at image_xscale - and on a tower image_xscale is +/-1 FACING only, because the art size had to come out of it for the click mask (LL-033). It would draw a full-size 192px tower with a 1px ring around it. (2) the .fsh takes its colour from v_vColour and IGNORES v_vColour on the sprite pixels (texture2D is added unmultiplied), so riding the colour on image_blend would steal the level tint for the ring and drop it from the body - and image_blend is simultaneously the hover glow colour, the reflection colour and the water copy colour. PLAN: add an explicit outlineColor uniform and mix it against the tinted body (mix(outlineColor, base*v_vColour, originAlpha)); add the four DIAGONALS to the neighbour sum, because the current kernel is a plus and corners notch at 1-2px; draw through scr_draw_self_scaled() so the size, the facing sign, image_blend and image_alpha all come from the one place that knows the idiom; check sprite_exists() BEFORE shader_set (LL-012 - a tower with no sprite is fatal, not a 0x0); take the thickness in SCREEN pixels and divide by draw_scale, so the 66x88 and 100x95 placeholder towers get the same edge as the 192x192 trios; and never return between shader_set and shader_reset - a missed reset leaves the shader bound and outlines the rest of the frame. NO NEW RESOURCE: the gm CLI has new-script and new-object but no new-shader, so a new shader would mean hand-editing .yy/.yyp (LL-009). shd_outline.fsh and .vsh are CRLF-only (36 and 20 lines) - byte-preserving edit, and GameMaker must not have the project open (LL-008). DONE 2026-10-15 (LL-045). It was DEAD CODE: shd_outline, scr_getOutlineShd() and scr_drawSelfOutlined() all existed and NOTHING had ever called the two scripts, so the outline machinery had never drawn a pixel - found by grepping the names outside their own files. Three faults were waiting inside it. (1) the helper ended in draw_self(), which draws at image_xscale, and on a tower that is +/-1 FACING only (LL-033) - it would have drawn a full-size 192px tower under a 1px ring. (2) the .fsh took its colour from v_vColour and then added the RAW texture, so the ring and the sprite TINT were the same variable and the tint was thrown away - and image_blend is also the hover glow colour, the reflection colour and the water copy colour. (3) there was no guaranteed shader_reset. Now: an explicit outlineColor uniform, the body keeps its tint (mix(outlineColor, body, originAlpha)), the four DIAGONALS added so corners do not notch, every guard BEFORE shader_set, shader_is_compiled() at setup so a compile failure is "no ring" rather than a half-drawn tower, and the thickness named in SCREEN pixels and divided by draw_scale so the 66x88 and 100x95 placeholder towers match the 192x192 trios. NO new resource: the CLI has new-script/new-object but no new-shader, so a new shader would have meant hand-editing .yy/.yyp (LL-009). shd_outline.fsh stayed CRLF-only (36 -> 54 lines) and every touched file kept its exact line endings.

tasks.title: find_all_range could never return more than one monster - `targets` was dead
tasks.needs: Reload the project, run any stage, and place a Slender Mandrake, Pina Collider or Cannon Tulip where several monsters are in range. In the Output window (global.devMode) look for lines reading "TOWER  cap 3  returned 3" - the cap and the count should match, bounded by how many are actually in range. "cap 3  returned 1" means the old build is still running (reload again); NO line at all means the tower never acquired targets.
tasks.notes: The loop read `array_last_index(_targets)` and then wrote `_targets[_ind]` - the index it had JUST READ. Writing only at the last index cannot change the last index, so the list could never grow past one entry whatever `qty` was: L(t+1) = max(L(t), L(t)) = L(t). So EVERY tower was single-target and `targets` was inert - Mandrake 375 nominal dps was really 125, Pina 2000 was really 200, Tulip 150 was really 30. The starters were documented as covering "cheap DPS, damage over time, multi-target and area damage"; two of those roles did not exist. Fixed: append, sort nearest-first, cap at qty, and the non-array sentinel preserved because scr_tower_shoot tests `!is_array(target)` to decide "return to idle" - an empty array would have read as a valid list and left towers swinging at the air. tasks.title: The level ring's palette: red/orange/green/blue, 25% at rest, 75% on hover, additive

Say whether the four colours read against the ground art - additive means they ADD light, so a pale ring over pale ground is the weakest case and the one to look at - and whether the grey-to-white image_blend tint stays. Also look at a tower standing IN water: the ring should stop at the waterline.
tasks.notes: The outline is about to become the ONLY thing that says what level a tower is - the size stops moving (choose-upgrade-scale) - so this card decides how readable an upgrade is. Levels 2-10 need a colour each; level 1 has none, by your instruction. The cap is 5 + mastery, so 10 is the real ceiling and nine colours covers the whole campaign. CONSTRAINTS, all from things the game already uses: red and green are the placement ghost (spr_noPlace) at the exact moment the player is looking at a tower, c_yellow is the damage/range float text, c_lime is the level number on the tower card, and orange is the despawn light. The ring also has to read against grass, dirt AND the blue water, which is what makes the blue rungs the ones to check first. PROPOSED (mine, and only a starting point): L2 #4FD16B green, L3 #2FD3C0 teal, L4 #35B6FF azure, L5 #5C8CFF blue, L6 #8A6BFF indigo, L7 #B95CFF violet, L8 #E85CD8 magenta, L9 #FF6FB0 pink, L10 #FFD24A gold - a cool to hot sweep with gold at the cap reading as maxed. The competing idea is a straight heat ramp (green, yellow, orange, red, white), which is more obviously stronger but spends red on a level cue. ALSO ON THIS CARD: the tint. Placement sets image_blend = c_gray and an upgrade lerps it to c_white, so a tower is already dimmer at level 1 than at level 10 - a second level signal that will make a coloured ring read duller on exactly the towers that need it most. Dropping it (placed towers become c_white, art at its true colours) is the recommendation; keeping it is a legitimate choice, it just has to be a choice. FIRST PASS SHIPPED 2026-10-15 (tower-level-look): the mechanism is in with the nine colours above, so this is a review of something you can look at rather than a question to answer blind. The tint is deliberately UNTOUCHED - dropping it changes the look of every tower on the map, and that is not a thing to decide on your behalf. One more thing worth a look while you are there: a tower standing IN water, where the ring should stop at the waterline rather than draw an edge along the crop. NAMED 2026-10-15 (this is the answer to the question the card was asking): red, orange, green and blue, one per rung, drawn additively at 25% opacity and 75% while the pointer is over the tower. SHIPPED the same day, and the mechanism changed to make it possible - see LL-046. The ring pass is now RING-ONLY (shd_outline writes alpha 0 on the art's own pixels) and the body is drawn before it by scr_drawSelfOutlined, because a blend mode belongs to the PASS and not to the thing you meant to blend: an additive pass that also drew the body would ADD the tower to the background instead of replacing it. The opacity rides on outlineColor's fourth component (draw_set_alpha() cannot reach a shader that writes gl_FragColor itself), and the blend mode is set LAST in scr_outline_begin - after every early return - and put back in scr_outline_end beside shader_reset(), because a leaked bm_add leaves the rest of the frame additive with no error to find it by. The four hues are make_colour_rgb(255,64,64) RED, (255,152,48) ORANGE, (72,224,96) GREEN, (64,144,255) BLUE - deliberately NOT c_red/c_green/c_blue, because GameMaker's c_green is (0,128,0) and a dark green barely registers when it is added rather than painted. Levels 6-10 (the mastery ladder) are still the first pass and are now their own card, tower-ring-mastery-palette. Four things to check: (1) no second, larger copy of the plant around it; (2) two towers with different art (a daisy and a Cannon Tulip) meet the surface at the SAME depth; (3) a LEFT-FACING tower in water is not upside down; (4) there is a dim mirrored reflection under the seam. Then say whether the sink is right - water_sink() in draw_water_shader.gml is the one number (8px now; 0 is 'on the water', 20+ is 'wading deep').
tasks.notes: Four defects, all one art change away from each other, all in the water draws (LL-043). obj_water/Draw_0 re-drew in-water TOWERS with draw_self(), which draws at image_xscale - but on a tower that is +/-1 FACING only and the size is draw_scale, so the submerged copy was 1.43x too big (and scr_drawLight had already been fixed for exactly this; the water pass was missed). The waterline was 0.8 of the CANVAS on a tower and 0.75 on a monster, which is a different WORLD DEPTH per sprite: the daisy's seam fell 3.1px above its base, spr_t3's 3.2px, a monster's 7.5px - three waterlines from three numbers that were each 'the same idea'. obj_tower/Draw_0 passed the FACING SIGN into _sy as well as _sx, and draw_sprite_part_ext reads a negative yscale as 'upside down AND anchored from there', so a left-facing in-water tower was flipped and dropped ~220px. And scr_drawReflections had been ported DISABLED (its only caller was commented out, with _statObj, a GM8 global that no longer exists) and was wrong in three ways by the time anyone looked. Fixed by deriving the seam from the ORIGIN (water_line_keep) with the depth in SCREEN pixels (water_sink), so all four callers agree by construction; water_line_report prints one line per instance. NOT yet seen in the game - which is why this card is in review. VALIDATED IN PLAY and archived on rayu's instruction. The waterline is one number now - water_sink() - and everything standing in water derives its seam from the ORIGIN rather than from a fraction of its own canvas, so a daisy, a Tulip and a monster all meet the surface at one depth instead of at 0.8 of whatever canvas they happen to have. The four things that were checked (a plant standing in water, its reflection meeting the surface, the submerged copy the right size, and the left-facing tower not flipped) all read right. draw_water_shader.gml holds water_sink()/water_line_keep()/water_line_report(), and it is still the ONE number to turn if the depth is ever wrong.

tasks.title: 15 + 5 wave rule and the per-biome difficulty curve
tasks.notes: Waves are a rule now (15 in stage 1, +5 a stage, in every biome) and the ramp is per biome: 1.00 on wave 1 everywhere, rising to the region's curve_end on the last wave, bent quadratically because money grows with the square of the wave. This replaced 2^(wave/5-2) + 0.2(w-1), which hit x1036 at wave 60.

tasks.title: Every rig carries an attack slot nobody plays: the gate is a place, not an enemy
tasks.notes: The ten rigs arrived with walk/idle/attack/die, and scr_zomb_art plays three of them: walk while path_free, idle while blocked, die in scr_zomb_death. Slot 2 is never played, because a monster here does not fight - it walks to the gate and takes a life, and scr_zomb_updatePosition returns once dying. So either the slot stays decorative (art_descriptions.md section 3.2 now says so in as many words) or the gate grows a real engage step: stop on arrival, attack for N seconds, then lose the life. That is a design decision plus scr_level_wait/scr_zomb_death work, not a drawing job - and it moves the leak clock, so run gm balance sim on stage 1-1 before and after.

tasks.title: Corpses lie on the path: the ground is the sprite origin, so the measured offset is deleted
tasks.needs: Reload GameMaker, run with global.devMode = true, and kill a few creatures in region 1 stage 1: Grumble-Mulch, then the mid boss Tusk-A-Lot and the end boss Sub-Zero. Each body must now PLAY ITS DIE SHEET (it topples forward over 0.8 s) and settle ON the path it died on, not below it, and the Gardener (a boss at scale 0.2) must walk on the ground instead of 2 px into it. The log must show one kill line per death with die=spr_grumble_die / die=spr_tusk_die / die=spr_zero_die - a line reading die=NONE (keeps the walk art) means a row lost its die slot. What would prove it wrong: a corpse that still walks into its grave, one that sinks, or one that floats above the path.
tasks.notes: The shift lived in objects/obj_mon/Draw_0.gml: y += zomb_ground_offset(sprite_index) * abs(image_yscale) before the draw and y -= _off after it. zomb_ground_offset() answered (sprite_get_height-1) - sprite_get_bbox_bottom: the empty canvas padding under the art, a number with nothing to do with where the feet are (the art bottom appears at y + bbox_bottom - yorigin; canvas height never enters it). That padding is the room reserved for the body to lie down - 22 empty rows in the Bell-Ringer 175 px sheet, 17 in the Bog-Wader - and one bbox serves all sixteen frames besides, so the number was the sheet and not the frame. Measured from the PNGs, die frame 0 stands within 5 px of walk frame 0 on all fifteen rigs (worst Bog-Wader -2/+7, Zero +7/+2, Grumble -4/+3), and the LAST die frame lies 23 px below the feet on Tusk and Zero - the fall pivots on the origin by design. So the art was right and the code was wrong: the correction is deleted, not re-derived. Screen px it removed, for the ten rows that actually play a die sheet: Shroud 28, Newly-Turned 10, Sandblasted 7, Bog-Wader 6.8, Bell-Ringer 6.6, Gardener 2.6, Root-Bound 1.5, Foreman-Rustlung 0.8, Harvester 0.6, Orchid-Widow 0.35; and every creature also stood 0-2.5 px inside the path it WALKED, on every frame (Grumble-Mulch 2.0, Newly-Turned 2.5, Gardener 2.0, Sandblasted 1.75, Professor-Cerebrisk 1.5). zomb_ground_offset had exactly one caller, so it is deleted rather than left dead. LL-078 added. Two tests: ZombieRigTests.test_the_die_frame_stands_where_the_walk_frame_stands decodes frame 0 of every rig walk and die sheet and demands the ground contact agrees within 6 canvas px; test_nothing_moves_a_monster_off_its_origin_to_reach_the_ground fails on any vertical y shift in the monster Draw or any zomb_ground_offset in the art script (both mutation-checked). Suite 319 -> 321. 2026-10-24 (second pass, after rayu played it): the corpse was not sinking - it was still playing its WALK frames, because this row set had no die slot at all (LL-079). Region 1 stage 1 is Grumble-Mulch plus the bosses Tusk-A-Lot and Sub-Zero, three of the five unrigged rows, which is exactly why the fall was invisible there.

tasks.title: Five creatures have a 16-frame die sheet the game never plays, so they vanish with no fall
tasks.notes: WIRED, not deleted - and it was the bug behind 'the walk animation plays as the zombies die'. All four sets of all five creatures were on disk AND registered in the .yyp as 16 distinct frames each, and the die sheets are real falls: the body top comes down 68-81 canvas px from a standing height of 140-157 (Grumble -149 -> -68 relative to the origin, Dome -149 -> -69, Professor -157 -> -76, Tusk -146 -> -67, Zero -140 -> -63) while the lowest pixel passes the origin (+3 -> +17, +6 -> +23, +5 -> +19, +6 -> +31, +2 -> +23). The rows still passed a one-element array(spr_x_walk), and zomb_art_play answers false for an empty slot and leaves the previous animation cycling - so the corpse walked in place for 0.8 s and vanished. REGION 1 STAGES 1-5 SPAWN NOTHING BUT THESE FIVE (stage 1-2 [0], every boss pair [0,1], stage 3 adds spawner 1, stage 5 spawner 2; Newly-Turned only joins at stage 6), so the first stage anyone plays was 100% affected while the ten wired rigs sat behind five stages. Fixed: four slots in all five rows; the kill line now prints die=<sprite> or die=NONE (keeps the walk art), so a silent fallback can never again pass for a broken animation; RIGGED grew from ten rows to fifteen; test_the_originals_keep_a_single_walk_sprite - which pinned the missing art as correct - is replaced by test_every_creature_row_is_in_the_rig_table, an equality between the rig table and the spawn table. LL-079 added.

tasks.title: The monster flow is an enum + switch and DEATH is a state, not a flag polled inside the walk
tasks.needs: Reload GameMaker with global.devMode = true and play a stage. Kill a monster WHILE IT IS RISING (every monster rises for 60 steps at the start of a wave): it must topple where it was killed and never stand up first. Then check any kill in the log: META  [ZOMB] die <id>  art=spr_..._die  frames=16  image_speed=0.33  steps=48 once, then about 0.8s later META  [ZOMB] corpse gone <id> after N steps (the sheet wrapped) with N between 46 and 50, and NO frame of the walk cycle between the last fall pose and the body vanishing. No corpse may slide along its path after the death line. What would prove it wrong: a META  [LEVEL] kill with no ZOMB die line after it, art= naming a walk sprite on a creature that has a die sheet, corpse gone saying (the step clock) on a normal rig, a zombie standing up after being killed mid-emerge, a WARNING die art did not advance line, or a wave that will not end because a corpse stayed.
tasks.notes: Death used to be a flag polled at the top of scr_zombie_path, so (1) a monster killed during EMERGE was never checked - the emerge has no life test and its last step requested the walk - and could stand up and walk; (2) the fall clock started one step after the kill, so the sheet wrapped to frame 0 and frame 0 was DRAWN once (a one-frame standing blip); (3) Alarm_0, armed by Collision_obj_tower whenever a monster brushes a tower, which is where kills happen, could path_start a corpse and the follower dragged it; (4) the destroy used round(ZOMB_DIE_SECS*fps) instead of watching the animation, so it agreed with the sprite only by coincidence. Now scr_zomb_state owns the flow: enum ZOMB_STATE {NONE,EMERGE,PATH,DIE} with request/apply (scr_zomb_request / scr_zomb_begin) like scr_level_state, and scr_zomb_step checks the life BEFORE the switch and returns, so no state can miss a death. scr_zomb_death is the kill only (money, points, kill line, path_end, alarm[0] = -1, request DIE); scr_zombie_die owns the fall and destroys when image_index wraps - last pose drawn, frame 0 never - with the step count as the clock for a rig with no die slot, plus a logged 2x backstop. Alarm_0 exits on a dying monster. 9 new tests in MonsterStateMachineTests, all mutation-checked (7 of 7 mutations caught); 322 to 331. Recorded as LL-080.

tasks.title: Monster art is a named rig struct on a roster, not a positional array copied per instance
tasks.needs: Reload GameMaker, set global.devMode = true and play a stage. At boot the log must print one RIG walker/boss N <creature> slots=4 walk=spr_<x>_walk idle=spr_<x>_idle attack=spr_<x>_attack die=spr_<x>_die line per creature (15 of them) and NO none anywhere - the all-none roster WAS the bug (LL-083). On every kill the corpse must fall with its die sheet: RIG die <id> ... was=spr_<x>_walk now=spr_<x>_die changed=1, and META [ZOMB] die art=spr_<x>_die; body gone ~48 steps later (the sheet wrapped). What would prove it wrong: die=none or walk=none on any creature, a has NO die slot warning, changed=0 with now= a walk sprite, or a wave that never ends.
tasks.notes: LL-081: the rig became one read-only struct per creature, read BY NAME (mon_rig_slot/mon_rig_play), built once in scr_setupSpawning - but mon_rig_pick type-tested its ZOMB_ANIM slot with is_real(), and is_real answers FALSE for enum values, which are stored as int64s (the manual is_real note; LL-034 landmine struck again). EVERY rig was therefore built with walk/idle/attack/die = -1 while slots=4 - no monster was ever dressed, no corpse ever fell, and the boot trace said slots=4 walk=none for all fifteen creatures, the evidence sitting unread in the run log (LL-083). The is_real line is deleted; the bounds checks are the real guards, and that one deletion unblocks the roster, dress-at-birth, the heal, the emerge switch and the fall. zomb_art_sprite/zomb_art_play stay deleted; zomb_rig() self-heal and the ungated RIG traces unchanged.

log.what: Compacted six guides and ten GML files, removing duplicated history and conversational prose while preserving executable lines and line-ending styles. Fixed four roadmap links. Validation: 341 tests OK (3 skipped), 823 resources round-trip, balance, Markdown, and progress checks green.
Fixed the per-frame 'Unable to find instance for object index 1': a persistent instance whose dependency did not persist.
One level object (GameLevelData) and a deploy gate the level data can pass, so the world map cannot offer a stage that has no data.
Waves became a rule (15 + 5 a stage, all six biomes) and the ramp became region_data's per-biome curve, replacing the exponential that hit x1036 at wave 60.
The 4.4 ladder: a level is base x ladder and never compounds; cap and floor come from the garden; rungs are re-priced and selling refunds 60% of what went in.
The difficulty columns are read at last - hp, speed, count, money and starting money. Before this, Brutal only paid better; it never fought harder.
Found that 4.3's prices and 4.4's ladder disagree: a rung returns +0.16 dps per unit of money against +1.00 for another placement. Written up as economy.md 4.6 and left open for a decision.
Built the progress tracker: progress.json as the source, PROGRESS.md and progress.html generated from it, and gm progress check failing when the three disagree.
Tightened the tracker: a backlog card may no longer be awaiting a person, because the top strip filled with parked work within the hour (LL-023).

Fixed the tower-card crash: the Phase 1 economy refactor called tower_upgrade_price() and tower_sell_refund() but never defined them, so selecting a tower died at _levelControl/Step_0.gml:94. Both now live in tower_levels.gml beside tower_rung_cost().

Closed the 'commit the curve work' card: every file it said was untracked is already committed in HEAD and git status is clean, so the card had gone stale. Noted the LL-024 lesson (a call to an undefined function reports as a variable read in the CALLER's scope).

Zombies marched north through the walls. obj_mon/Draw_72 (Pre Draw) and Draw_73 (Post Draw) both subtracted z_climb*2-12 - a draw-only offset applied twice - and Alarm_0 threw the live path away (path_end + path_clear_points) before asking the grid for a new one, so one failed re-path left the monster with no path and nothing rewriting its y. Draw_73 now restores the offset, and scr_path_replace() probes a scratch path and only commits on success, so the last valid path is kept. Also made the tower's grid block and its clear the same rectangle. Written up as LL-025.

Fixed the Input._objSwitch crash. key_type holds function references, but scr_save_keys persisted it through ds_list_write, which cannot represent a function - so on the next launch key_type came back as numbers and Input/Step_0's script_execute() ran whatever script that number indexed (scr_drawTimerExt, which reads the unrecovered _objSwitch). scr_save_keys no longer saves key_type, scr_load_keys rejects a non-callable loaded key_type and keeps the freshly built one, Input/Step_0 only script_execute()s a callable, and scr_drawTimerExt resolves _objSwitch with asset_get_index and bails when absent. Written up as LL-026.

Pathfinding was still wrong after LL-025. mp_grid_add_rectangle and mp_grid_add_instances floor BOTH edges and iterate INCLUSIVELY, so the tower's x+-cell_w/2 rectangle - whose far edge lands exactly on the next cell boundary - marked a 2x2 block instead of the one 32x32 cell it occupies (and any instance whose bbox far edge hit a boundary over-blocked the same way, which is how the walled pen's one-cell exit could seal). Fixed: obj_tower Create/Destroy block and clear exactly one cell by index (grid_col/grid_row); obj_tower_edit blocks one cell for the candidate and one per existing blocker; a new scr_grid_block_instances() replaces mp_grid_add_instances over the live grid in scr_resetDrawPath and obj_mon/Alarm_0. Written up as LL-027.

Replaced every script_execute() in the project (14 call sites across 12 files) with a new run_script(script_name, target=noone, arguments_list=[]). It returns undefined unless the name passes !is_undefined() && is_callable(); when target != noone and instance_exists(target) it re-binds with method(target, script_name) so the call runs in that instance's scope, otherwise it runs in the caller's scope as script_execute() did. GML has no argument spread, so arguments_list is forwarded through a switch on array_length (0..4 - the widest site, for_grid, passes 4) and a longer list logs via scr_meta_log instead of failing silently. Sites: Input/Step_0 (the LL-026 dispatch), scr_runState, scr_stpButton, scr_updateReciever, the for_* iterators, and _oTextInput Create/Step/Draw. run_script is not a GameMaker built-in (LL-005 checked); LL-026's guard rails now point at it.

Chased the Input crash that appeared after the run_script migration: 'Variable obj_spawn.time_keeper not set before reading it' from scr_drawSwitchTimer, called by Input/Step_0 -> run_script. Decoding the save file showed [KeyInputData] 1 still holds the listeners as type-marker-15 values (100417/100415), i.e. ds_list_write/read DOES round-trip a function reference - it comes back as a value that is STILL CALLABLE, so scr_load_keys' is_callable() guard passed and key_type was replaced by the stale array; the dispatch then ran whatever script the old handle now indexes (scr_drawTimerExt for LL-026, scr_drawSwitchTimer once run_script added a script). run_script()'s guard cannot see it: the value is not undefined, not a number and not non-callable. Fix: scr_load_keys/scr_load_gamepad no longer read slot 1, and scr_save_keys/scr_save_gamepad blank it so an older build cannot read it either; the live save file was purged too. Written up as LL-028, which corrects LL-026's premise that the value comes back as a plain number.

Playtest validation: 'Plants block one 32x32 grid cell, not a 2x2' - the pathing works as of the last test. The reloaded build also ran without the Input dispatch crash, so the saved-key_type fixes hold. That closes fix-tower-cell-footprint, fix-zombie-north-drift, fix-keytype-dispatch, fix-saved-keytype, run-script-dispatch and gm-reload-verify; the validated build is committed (e924703).

Chased the playtest report that some towers stick in the attack animation. scr_tower_shoot left the attack state only on `state_time == frame_number`, but frame_number = room_speed/data[TOWER.fire_rate] is a FLOAT once fire_rate is scaled - the level ladder multiplies it by 1.04/1.08/... (tower_levels.gml) and placement folds in the garden floor and clover bonuses - so a base 3/s tower is 19.23 frames at L2. state_time is an integer, so that equality could never hold and the tower looped the attack sprite forever (and stopped dealing damage). Fixed: the state exits on >= frame_number, damage and particles fire once via did_damage/did_particles flags with clamped frames, and the target list is re-validated every frame so a target that dies or leaves range mid-swing returns the tower to idle. Written up as LL-029.

Chased the report that the Daisy Pusher plays its idle and return animations about three times too fast after its sprite was swapped for the 5-frame spr_daisy_*_192x trio. Two of the three tower states set image_speed - a SPEED - where a duration was meant: the idle loop was 0.25 and the return was 1, so the period scaled with the frame count (15 frames at 0.25 is 60 steps; 5 frames at 0.25 is 20). The attack was already frame-count independent because it divided by frame_number, which is exactly why the bug looked like bad art. Fixed by asking for a PERIOD everywhere: new scr_animSpeedForSteps(sprite, steps) returns the image_speed that plays a sprite through once in N steps whatever its frame count, and normalises the sprite's declared speed type (image_speed is a multiplier, not frames-per-step); new scr_tower_animSpeed(slot, steps) is the ONE place a tower's speed is set, and logs the period once per animation per tower; the durations live as anim_seconds on obj_tower (1.00s idle / 0.25s return = the periods the old 15-frame trio played at); sprite_list is now indexed by a new TOWER_ANIM enum instead of 0/1/2 literals; and the return state exits on state_time >= anim_steps rather than on image_index, which fired up to a frame early at a fractional speed. obj_tower_edit's placement ghost no longer relies on image_single (a GM8 variable that does not exist in GMS2) and holds frame 0. Written up as LL-030.

Chased the request that towers mirror to face their target. obj_tower/Step_0 now calls the new scr_tower_faceTarget(target) once per step, after scr_runState has refreshed target, and mirrors with the idiom image_xscale = -abs(image_xscale) / abs(image_xscale) that scr_zomb_updatePosition already uses for monsters (LL-012). The helper handles every shape target takes - instance_nearest gives an instance or noone, find_all_range gives an array or the integer -1 - faces the NEAREST valid one, holds the last facing when there is nothing to face, and ignores a target within 2px of the tower so a monster in the cell directly above or below cannot strobe the sprite; it writes and logs only on a turn. Two latent traps surfaced with the flip: the upgrade tween wrote a bare positive image_xscale (which un-mirrored the tower on upgrade) and image_yscale = image_xscale (which becomes NEGATIVE once the scale can be negative, drawing the tower upside-down) - both fixed, magnitudes unchanged. scr_drawLight builds the shadow silhouette from sprite_width/sprite_xoffset and ignored image_xscale, so it mirrors now too, which also corrects left-walking zombie shadows. LL-012 extended with the three ways a flip dies.

Chased the report that with no towers the zombies vanish a few seconds into every wave, the lives counter never moves and the wave still rewards the player. One mechanism could do it: the anti-softlock valve in scr_level_wait fired on ELAPSED TIME (6 s after the wave finished spawning) and destroyed EVERY live monster. A stopwatch cannot tell a monster that is walking from one that is stuck, and scr_zomb_pathSpeed puts a zombie at about 0.75 px/step (path_start passes an absolute speed) so it needs 20-45 s to cross a stage - the valve was not a net under the wave, it was the end of the wave. Because the monsters were deleted mid-route, the two arrival tests in scr_zomb_updatePosition never ran, lose_life() never fired, level_leaked stayed 0, Untouched was still earned and scr_level_clear paid seeds and clovers: the leak -> life -> game over mechanic was being discarded silently, and the leak path printed nothing at all, which is why it read as a missing mechanic rather than a bug. The valve now fires on evidence about the monster and only for that monster: scr_zomb_updatePosition counts steps in which path_position does not change (the path follower own progress report, which - unlike x/y - cannot be fooled by an instance that has lost its path and is drifting, LL-025), and scr_level_wait clears a monster that has not advanced for 5 s, logging path_free and path_retry and setting level_forced. Five seconds sits above the ~2 s obj_mon/Alarm_0 needs to escalate to the tower-ignoring escape grid, and a ten-minute per-wave latch (>= plus a one-shot flag, never ==, LL-029) keeps roadmap 4.4.1 promise that a stage can never hang. Every fate is now labelled exactly once in the log - kill / leak / valve - plus one line per monster giving path length, px/step and the projected walk time, so future thresholds are derived from the log rather than guessed. Written up as LL-031 and documented in systems_overview 4.3.1.

Split the tower art's size away from image_xscale, because a collision mask scales with image_xscale and the tower's click mask therefore arrived at half size. obj_tower already carried spr_tower_click_region (32x64: one cell wide, two cells tall) and it was correct; obj_tower/Create_0 drew the art with image_xscale = image_yscale = 0.5, so the mask was handed to the game as 16x32. The size moved into a new draw_scale (0.5 placed, 0.25 for the placement ghost), image_xscale/image_yscale are now +/-1 FACING ONLY, and a new scr_draw_self_scaled() is the one place that draws at the art's size and re-applies the facing sign. Every consumer of the size followed: scr_drawLight's shadow silhouette (guarded on the instance having a draw_scale, so monsters are unchanged), scr_drawGlowOutline (the halo now takes the size), draw_self_part (optional _sx/_sy, so its existing callers behave identically) and the upgrade tween, which now writes draw_scale and can no longer un-mirror a tower. The step-1 click box was deleted: Step_1 asks the mask itself with position_meeting, and _levelControl tie-breaks two stacked towers by the one whose own cell holds the pointer. In the same session all seven music tracks were mapped to their regions in music_data - mus_title plus mus_world1..mus_world6 - with the mapping read off each file's estimated tempo rather than assumed, and the brief's wiring table corrected: mus_world3 and mus_world4 are Desert and Jungle, not retired. Written up as LL-033. (fix-tower-click-mask)

Made the placement ghost ask the GRID instead of a collision mask. obj_tower_edit/Step_0 decided whether the cell under the ghost was taken with position_meeting(x, y, obj_tower), which reads the tower's 32x64 click mask - so the cell ABOVE a tower went red, while obj_tower/Create_0 blocks exactly one cell of LEVEL.path_grid and two towers are allowed to stack. It now asks the grid it is about to write into - mp_grid_get_cell(LEVEL.path_grid, (x + cell_w) div cell_w, (y + cell_h) div cell_h) != 0 - which is the same arithmetic obj_tower/Create_0 and scr_grid_block_instances use, plus the _spawn test that was already there (the spawn is not in the grid at all, and _spawn is also the parent of obj_wall, whose 32x32 art covers one cell, which backstops the part of the deploy countdown before scr_resetDrawPath puts the walls into the grid). The refusal now names its reason - META [PATH] placement refused: <why> - where it used to click, thud and vanish in silence, so a wrong-looking cell is one log line rather than a hunt. Folded into LL-033, whose mask caused both the tiny click area and the lying ghost. (fix-tower-click-mask)

Fixed the silence on every stage, and it was not the music. rayu's runtime log (`GameMakerStudio2/debug.log`) had one line: `META  [MUSIC] region 1 "Wilted Sprouts" has no track yet - playing nothing` - the right region and the right title, so the table and music_for_region() were fine and only `_music.sound` was rejected. The guard at the top of scr_music_start_level tested it with `!is_real(_sound) || _sound < 0`, and is_real() asks 'is this a plain number' while an asset reference is not one - so is_real(mus_world1) is false for a perfectly good sound and the guard refused EVERY region theme. The menu theme survived because obj_title and the Menu reach audio_play_sound_on() without passing through the guard. The guard now tests the two values music_data actually documents (-1 for 'not generated yet', undefined for 'no row') and the refusal says WHICH fired, the play line prints typeof(_sound) so the representation is on the record rather than assumed, and the loop-point pair 0.0/0.0 is no longer set for a whole-track loop (loop = true already repeats the track, and 0.0/0.0 depends on the runtime reading 'loop end 0' as 'end of file'). The asset was cleared on the way: mus_world1.yy is byte-identical to mus_world2.yy apart from the duration, and the IDE's asset cache held a valid converted mus_world1.wav with <Duration>163.53</Duration> beside it. Written up as LL-034, with the guard rail 'never ask a TYPE question about an asset'. (audio-region-music)

Fixed the in-water crash my own optional arguments caused. obj_mon/Draw_0 calls draw_self_part(0,0,1,0.75,0) - five arguments - while draw_self_part declares seven (argument0..argument6), and the optional _sx/_sy were being detected with `(argument_count > 5) ? argument5 : image_xscale`. The argument list is sized to the DECLARED arity and the unpassed parameters are padded with undefined, so argument_count was not 5, the ternary took the argument5 branch, and the next line multiplied by undefined: `undefined value at gml_Script_draw_self_part (line 33) - _x = x - sprite_get_xoffset(sprite_index)*_sx`, every frame a monster was in water. The error text itself proves the mechanism - 'undefined value' (arithmetic on undefined, so the slot EXISTS) rather than 'not set before reading it' - and image_xscale cannot be the culprit because obj_mon only ever assigns it real numbers (0, +/-abs, base_scale * _t, +/-base_scale, with base_scale 1 from Create or 0.25/0.5 from scr_level_spawn). scr_meta_log(_tag) declares one parameter and its loop prints all ten arguments, so argument_count = max(declared, passed) fits both cases; every other argument_count user in the project declares ZERO parameters, which is exactly why nothing else ever broke. The test is now is_undefined(argument5)/is_undefined(argument6) - the project's own 'not there' question, and independent of how argument_count is computed - with the defaults unchanged (image_xscale carries the monster's size AND sign, as the original sprite_xoffset code assumed). scr_drawGlowOutline carried the same brittle shape (argument_count > 0) and was fixed with it. obj_mon/Draw_0 keeps its short call on purpose: it is the test of the default path. Written up as LL-035. (fix-tower-click-mask)

Added a dev-only curve diagnostic so the wave ramp and the tower ladder are visible in the log instead of after a sixty-wave playtest. New script scr_curve, called ONCE from scr_level_start on stage entry. It prints one CURVE line per biome (m(1) and m(last) plus the reference monster hp at both ends - m(1) must be 1.00 in every row, in all six biomes), then, for the current stage, the route length in px and the mean terrain height z sampled from ground_map exactly the way scr_zomb_pathSpeed samples it, then the bite at wave 1 and at the last wave for Normal and Brutal. bite = required dps / available dps: required is count * hp / walk_seconds (per-monster traversal - the agreed queue-drain test), available is the money earned by that wave times the best placement dps per dollar in the loadout. It also prints place vs rung dps-per-dollar, which is economy.md 4.6's inequality in two numbers, so econ-rung-price can be decided from the log. Every read is guarded (LL-002 - a log line that throws aborts the Step) and the whole thing is gated on devMode. One real trap fixed on the way: the dps-per-money helper first took its two outputs as arguments, but GML passes a scalar BY VALUE, so it now returns a struct. This is the tool curve-playtest was waiting for: the LEVEL lines never showed the curve at all. (curve-diagnostic)

Built the headless balance tester the plan called P1, and put python -m gm balance {tables,route,project,check} on the toolkit. It reads every table out of the GML (region_data, difficulty_data, stage_data, tower_levels, the roster, the monster banks, the run constants) through a small GML parser, so a knob moved in GML moves the tester and there is no third source of truth to drift (LL-021). It rebuilds the route and the slot set from rooms/rm_test: 2048x1024, 27 walls, six spawns and one despawn are fixed, and the terrain - which IS re-rolled every launch, create_perlin_grid(random_get_seed())) - only moves walk speed, because obj_tower/Create_0 sets inWater and Draw_0 only uses it to sink the sprite. So the route (1779px mean over six spawns), the slots (282) and "how many towers this income buys" are all exactly reproducible. 43 new tests, 75 in the suite, all green. (balance-tester)

The tester immediately disagreed with the panel, and the panel is the one that is wrong. Three flaws, all in scr_curve_report's available = min(money/price, slots) x best dps: it prices every tower at the best dps-per-dollar one (Pina Collider, $100) so on waves 1-11 - purse $30 to $93 - it buys NOTHING and prints "?", while the shop sells $5 towers; it multiplies by targets = 10 as if ten monsters were inside a 75px range at once when they spawn 0.5s apart and walk ~1.26px a step (about 37px apart on an 1840px route, so two or three, not ten); and it credits a tower with full dps along the whole route when it only fires while a monster is in range - 9% to 15% of the route on 1-1. Fixing all three is what made the retune check out: the old cap of 30 now reads bite 1.32 with HIGH waves from 13, which is the leak that started this, and the retuned 13 reads a worst of 0.57. Filed as a decision rather than silently patched, because the panel may be wanted as a rough read-out with the tool as the authority. (balance-panel-supply)

With an honest model the three difficulty profiles come out of the game's own data as the three shapes that were asked for: Normal holds all the way (worst bite 0.57), Hard barely holds (0.88), Brutal breaks on the last wave (0.93). Those bands are the tool's PROPOSED reading and nothing in the game encodes them, so they are on the board for Rayu to confirm or replace with outcome bands - leaks, hearts left, idle money - which is what the sim (P2, filed as balance-sim) will measure. (balance-feel-targets)

A second finding the tool handed over for free: wave 1 is below the curve band's own floor on every difficulty (bite 0.10 Normal, 0.15 Hard, 0.28 Brutal against a required 0.35). So the first wave of every stage in the game is trivial by the project's own rule - either the starting $25 is too generous, the 0.35 floor is wrong, or wave 1 is a tutorial wave the band should exempt. Filed, not fixed: it is a design call. (balance-wave1-trivial)

Two smaller findings filed with the numbers attached. scr_curve_walk_seconds applies the wave speed ramp unconditionally while scr_zomb_pathSpeed only applies it below 1.0 px/step - so on fast ground the panel slows the monster down and understates the demand by up to 13% of the walk. And the panel's difficulty list is [NORMAL, BRUTAL], so HARD is never projected at all despite being a fully wired column. Both one-line fixes, both left on the board because neither changes a number the player can see today. (balance-speed-ramp-divergence, balance-hard-not-projected)

Went looking at the tower arithmetic and found the reason the roster has no choices: `targets` does nothing. find_all_range read `array_last_index(_targets)` and then wrote `_targets[_ind]` - the index it had JUST READ - so the list could never grow past one entry. Provable from the code shape alone, so EVERY tower in the game was single-target: Mandrake 375 nominal dps was really 125, Pina 2000 was really 200, Tulip 150 was really 30. The two roles scr_tower_roster says the starters cover - multi-target and area damage - did not exist, and this is the deeper reason the curve panel was optimistic by an order of magnitude (LL-038). Fixed the list (append, sort nearest-first, cap at qty) while KEEPING the non-array sentinel that scr_tower_shoot relies on to return a tower to idle - an empty array would have read as a valid target list and left towers swinging at the air. Added a bounded dev-mode probe that prints the cap beside the count, so the fix can be seen rather than argued. Gates: roundtrip 674/0, 75 tests OK, braces balanced, no line-ending change (Create_0 is CRLF and stayed CRLF with its LF-only blank lines intact), progress green. (targets-cap-fix)

The tower arithmetic, measured: the ladder is wider than the income (prices span 5 to 100 while every coin in stage 1-1 is $122, of which $25 is the starting purse), so the player has 2 towers to choose from at wave 1, 3 from wave 4, and all four only from wave 12 of 15. Worse, the ratios are a RANKING rather than a set of trade-offs: nominal dps/$ spans 2.34 to 20.0 and single-target dps/$ spans 0.50 to 5.33, so on either measure there is one correct answer and it is a different tower. Agreed direction: prices 5/10/20/40, a start you can afford exactly one tower with, and kill money that climbs each wave - with those figures all four starters are live by wave 6. Filed rather than applied, because the fit should come from sim outcomes. Also found that raising the curve to compensate tears the difficulty columns apart (hp x2.5 vs money x1.5), so prices, curve and columns are ONE change. (economy-prices-rebalance, kill-money-ramp, difficulty-columns-vs-curve, balance-towers-report, balance-fit-from-sim)

Went to build the balance sim and started by checking its inputs against the game - which is where the biggest number of the session fell out: the fire period was charged TWICE per shot. A shot walks idle -> attack -> return, and the idle wait in scr_tower_normal was room_speed/fire_rate + time_offset, a WHOLE fire period, while scr_tower_shoot's own comment says 'the attack's length IS the fire rate' and spends another whole period. So the cycle was 2P + off + 15, not P: a Daisy Pusher (fire_rate 3, P = 20) swung every ~59 frames instead of ~20. Every tower dealt about a third of the dps on its card - and, the part that matters for pricing, NOT evenly: the fix is 1.51x for the Daisy and 1.86x for the Tulip, so the roster ORDER moves and this has to land before the prices are fitted. Fixed with one line (scr_tower_normal waits time_offset only), added a bounded probe that prints the MEASURED step gap between swings so the fix is seen rather than assumed, and wrote it up as LL-040. Two findings filed rather than fixed: the residual 1.3x-2x overstatement (the 0.25s return is not part of fire_rate) and scr_zombie_emerge resetting life to maxLife, which silently erases every shot fired at an emerging monster while making it the nearest target. Gates: roundtrip 674/0, 75 tests OK, braces balanced after the edit, mixed CRLF/LF preserved byte-for-byte in Create_0 and Step_0, no literal backslash-r, balance and progress green. (tower-fire-cycle-doubled, fire-rate-vs-animation-length, emerge-resets-life, targets-cap-fix)

The roster arithmetic is a command now, and it is the first read-out that charges the fire cycle. `gm balance towers` prints four dps figures per tower - card (damage x rate x targets, the shop), x1 (one target), deliv (x1 with the cycle charged, LL-040) and eff (deliv x coverage) - plus price per dps three ways, the seed/gate terms, and dominance on two axis sets. `gm balance afford` prints money_through against every price, wave by wave, so 'a tower is affordable' can be told apart from 'the player has a choice'. First results on 1-1: the roster DOES have a choice (Burning Ivy is the best value at $3.17 per delivered dps, Slender Mandrake the strongest at 13.9 eff dps) but the value spread is 2.3x and Pina Collider is dominated ON THE BOARD by Mandrake - cheaper and stronger - escaping only through its ten-target ceiling, which needs congestion nobody has shown exists. Also fixed a silent test loss found on the way: two geometry tests were indented inside the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block and had never run since the day they were written (LL-041); the suite reads 87 now, not 75. Gates: roundtrip 674/0, 87 tests OK, balance + progress green. (balance-towers-report, test-file-orphaned-tests, economy-prices-rebalance, balance-sim)

The sim exists, and it found something the closed form could not. `gm balance sim` steps a whole stage at 60fps: 30-frame spawns, boss MAX=1, emerges that REFRESH the life at frame 60, the idle/attack/return state machine with time_offset and fire_frame, the capped nearest-first target list, money paid in the frame a kill lands, a leak that costs a life and pays nothing, the 354-frame wave gate, and game over at zero lives. It reports per-wave fight/gate seconds, leaks, hearts, idle money, wasted swings, erased damage, and the widest target list any tower held. Three results: (1) BRUTAL IS EASIER THAN HARD - the difficulty money column is a step function, because round(1 x 1.25) is 1 and round(1 x 1.5) is 2, so hp per dollar is worst on Hard (LL-042); (2) Pina Collider's ten-target cap is unreachable - the widest list is 7, so its ceiling is ~7x and it stays dominated; (3) 41% of the stage is the between-wave gate and 24% of swings achieve nothing, of which the emerge reset is only ~3% of the hp. Also fixed three model errors found on the way: the tallest ground halves (z=12 walks like z=6), `policy.plan` now ranks on cycle-charged dps (which moved the closed form ~35% harsher - it is the pessimistic tool now, and the sim is the arbiter), and the deploy countdown is 3s + 5.9s + one frame. 101 tests, LL-042, economy.md 4.1 and checkpoints 13-14. (balance-sim, balance-sim-policy, difficulty-columns-vs-curve, economy-prices-rebalance)

The water draws were obeying numbers that had stopped describing the art, and nothing errored. Four defects, all one art change away from each other (LL-043): (1) obj_water/Draw_0 re-drew in-water TOWERS with draw_self(), which draws at image_xscale - on a tower that is +/-1 FACING only (LL-033) and the size is draw_scale, so the submerged copy was 1.43x too big; scr_drawLight had already been fixed for exactly this and the water pass was missed. (2) The waterline was 0.8 of the CANVAS on a tower and 0.75 on a monster, which is a different WORLD DEPTH per sprite - measured, the daisy met the water 3.1px above its base, spr_t3 3.2px and a monster 7.5px. (3) obj_tower/Draw_0 passed the FACING SIGN into _sy as well as _sx, and draw_sprite_part_ext reads a negative yscale as "upside down AND anchored from there", so a left-facing in-water tower was flipped and dropped ~220px - LL-012 one more time. (4) scr_drawReflections had been ported DISABLED: its only caller was commented out and passed _statObj, a GM8 global that does not exist in GMS2, and by the time anyone looked it was wrong in three ways. The fix is one function - water_line_keep() derives the seam from the sprite ORIGIN, with the depth named in SCREEN pixels (water_sink(), 8px) - and all four callers use it, so they agree by construction. water_line_report() prints one line per instance (canvas, origin as a fraction of it, scale, height left visible) so the numbers are readable instead of arguable. Not yet SEEN - the card is in review awaiting a reload.

Decided: an upgrade must never make a tower smaller. The size stops carrying the level - draw_scale frozen at the placed 0.5 - and a per-level outline colour carries it instead. Both options this card offered are rejected in favour of removing the signal (tower-level-look, tower-level-palette).

Revived the ported-but-never-called outline shader (LL-045). It was dead code with three faults inside: draw_self() at image_xscale (LL-033), a colour that came out of image_blend while the body tint was thrown away, and no guaranteed shader_reset. Now an explicit outlineColor uniform, diagonals for the corners, thickness in screen pixels, and shader_is_compiled() so a compile failure is a missing ring and not a broken frame.

The level is the ring now. draw_scale is frozen at the placed 0.5 (L2 used to come out 0.34, so every upgrade shrank the tower), level 1 has no ring, levels 2-10 have a colour each (tower_level_outline), the ring is drawn after the hover glow and never around it, and the two stale 0.70 comments that explained LL-043 are corrected to 2x at 0.5. The nine hues are a FIRST PASS for review.
Named the level ring's palette: red, orange, green, blue - one per rung, L2 to L5 - drawn additively at 25% opacity, 75% while hovering the tower.

Shipped it, and the ring pass had to become RING-ONLY to take a blend mode: the body is drawn first and normally, then the shader adds the ring over it. An additive pass that also drew the body would add the tower to the background instead of replacing it, and draw_set_alpha() cannot reach a shader that writes gl_FragColor - the opacity rides on outlineColor.a, and the blend mode is set after every early return and put back beside shader_reset (LL-046). Levels 6-10 split out as tower-ring-mastery-palette.

Hovering a plant now lights the 32x32 grid cell it stands on and prints its level above its head, white with a black outline. The cell is the FOOTPRINT the tower blocked (grid_col/grid_row, LL-027), not the art, which is up to three times its size; it is drawn in the grid's own Post Draw layer additively, so it is the grid brightening rather than a second overlay. tower_hovered is set in Step_0 where the hover is decided, so the cell, the level and the glow cannot name different towers. The label's height is the sprite's bbox top MINUS its origin - sprite_get_bbox_top() is measured from the canvas, not the origin, and the first version printed the number across the plant's stem (LL-047).

Found a second piece of ported dead code while checking for a bound shader: set_colorSwap_shader() and setup_color_swap() have no caller, and there is no shader resource for them to bind. Carded as backlog rather than fixed - it is a decision (build the shader or delete the scripts), not a bug.

Hovering a plant now says everything about it at once, and more quietly: the grid cell it stands on is halved (_fill 0.10 / _edge 0.25), its level prints above its head, and its range is a 3px additive white ring at 25% instead of the spr_towerRange decal. The decal filled the whole circle at 15% and was selection-driven, so a click washed out a large part of the garden; the ring is hover-driven and leaves everything inside and outside it legible. Ring, cell and level all read the same tower_hovered, so they cannot name different towers (LL-021). The card's range band still rings the selected tower so it is not a dead affordance.
