Found and fixed why the second stage never loaded. The bootstrap hung off Control/Create_0 - Control is persistent and is the first instance in the room, so Create ran once per launch, while _mainControl and everything it builds are non-persistent and died on Room End. Second entry: no main controller, so scr_main_startup never ran (no terrain) and the cutscene never ran (no _levelControl, no waves) - silently, because the room own placed instances do not depend on the boot. scr_level_boot() now runs from rm_test RoomCreationCode, which fires on every entry after every Create event; it is idempotent and logs a count. Control is non-persistent so the systems rebuild per stage, and scr_main_startup rebuilds the grid when it is missing, guards the 0/0 load divide and logs rows= when the reveal ends. fadeout() also gained an optional restart argument: room_goto to the current room is a no-op, so retry was silent. Written up as LL-049. Needs one run from rayu to confirm the boot line appears twice.

The save was being wiped on every load, and the proof was on disk: garden_meta.dat had towers:{"version":1.0}. scr_meta_merge looped over the DEFAULT keys, so every nested map ({} in the default) came back empty with a version stamp in it, while seeds, clovers and the loadout array survived - which is why it looked like a partial reset. The merge now reads the file, treats an empty default struct as an open map and a populated one as a fixed record, keeps scalars to their schema type, and lets the caller stamp the version. The load log prints the maps it used to lose, and gm save inspect reads a real save and fails on a stray stamp. LL-050. Schema is v2.

The options sliders read the mouse in the Draw event and only while the pointer was inside a 32px band, so a fast drag silently ended and 0/100 took a second pass; the volume also only applied on Return. scr_menu_slider now owns one geometry definition and a modal drag (grab on press, follow wherever the pointer goes, clamp, release), show_slider is draw-only, and every change is applied immediately - emitter gain for a volume, a throttled tick for Sound FX. audio_channel_num moved out of scr_resetSoundVolume into scr_applyClutter so a drag cannot reallocate channels per frame. LL-051.

Tower shadows flipped but did not follow the tower. scr_drawLight sized the silhouette from sprite_xoffset, which carries the image_xscale sign, so the box moved by 2*xoffset*draw_scale on every turn (97px on the 192px daisies) while the corner swap mirrored the texture inside it. The box is now built from abs(sprite_xoffset) and mirrored about the origin - which also fixes left-walking zombie shadows. LL-052.

Losing every life never reached the new level flow: LEVEL_STATE.FAILED existed and nothing requested it, so the legacy scr_main_normal ran scr_main_gameOver -> rm_score underneath and the meta layer never heard about the loss. scr_level_step now checks life before the switch, scr_level_failed pays nothing and takes nothing, writes the save, moves the run cursor and returns to the world map, and the legacy branch is gone. Both outcomes write global.level_result, the input the results screen needs. LL-053.

The two stage exits now open a results screen instead of the world map. It is a MENU_STATE, not a room, and it reads the global.level_result struct both exits already write - so a clear and a loss arrive with the same shape and the screen only reads outcome. Retry replays the same stage with the same difficulty and loadout, Next is enabled only on a clear and only when the next stage exists and is unlocked, and World Map is always there. A stale entry with no result logs and goes to the map. A results_leaving one-shot stops a second click during the fade from starting a second transition - the Retry and Next rects are measured from one geometry function, and the first draft had Next overlapping Map by 20px, which an if/else chain would have read as Next.

Continue is a real button again and it resumes at the run cursor. menu_button[1] was an explicit noone hole, so every read of it had to guard 0 = object index 0; it is a live button now, with Start moved up one row so Options and Quit keep their y and nothing sits on the Return button. The grey-out gate moved from file_exists of the legacy test.data - which nothing writes - to scr_run_started(), which asks for the meta file, the only thing a deploy or a stage exit writes. Pressing it sets region, stage, difficulty and global.loadout from run_get() and fades into the stage room.

The far-right shadow was the SECOND signed term, not the first one coming back. sprite_width is sprite_get_width * image_xscale, so on a left-facing tower it is negative and the flip branch (l = bx + xo - w) laid the box 48..144px to the RIGHT of the plant - while the un-mirrored branch, which uses w in the other direction, stayed correct. abs(sprite_width)/abs(sprite_height) fixes it, and a one-off SHADOW  flip line now prints w, h, xo and the box per instance so the sign is one grep away. LL-052 amdended with the second half and the completed rule: all four sprite_* size/origin variables carry the sign.

A slow tower could not fire, for three reasons that all said the fire period is the animation length: the swing WAS room_speed/fire_rate (600 frames for the Pina Collider), the damage frame sat at the END of it, and the swing was cancelled the moment the target left range - which a zombie does in about a hundred frames. On top of that the timer only existed inside the swing. Now attack_timer ticks in every state in obj_tower/Step_0 (so an idle tower is READY), attack_cycle = period + return + stagger (the cycle LL-040 and the closed form already assume, so no fast tower moves), the swing is min(period, 0.35s) of art, and a started swing commits. tower_levels owns the three numbers and the balance sim/tables read them. One finding moved and the test says so: the state machine now matches the idealised cycle instead of being slower, so the closed form is no longer conservative by a few frames - it is exact for a tower that always has a target, and still an upper bound for every real one.

LEVEL_STATE.CLEAR is a sequence, not a five-frame hop to the fade. On entry every wave is already stopped, the ghost/card/Up Next box/wave banner are removed and the stage takes no input; the HUD fades through one level_ui_alpha (stat inventory, build list, speed buttons) while the camera flies out to the largest view of the room that keeps the port aspect, wheel and drag suppressed. At 0.70s spr_level_complete comes up at 80% and grows to 100% over exactly 3.00s, centred, at 60% of the port height measured on the ART bbox - then the 0.8s fade to rm_menu, which opens RESULTS. The clock is delta_time, because fast-forward sets room_speed 180 and a frame count would make it one second. Every beat is one function, so it can be retimed in one place.

The HP bar could draw with a NEGATIVE width because obj_mon/Draw_73 fed an unclamped life/maxLife to lerp - a ratio below zero extrapolates the fill to the LEFT of the black bar. It is not a rounding case: scr_do_damage subtracts the whole hit and scr_zomb_death only runs inside scr_zombie_path, so a kill by a tower that steps later in the same frame draws one frame below zero; during EMERGE scr_zombie_emerge restores life = maxLife only at step 60, so an overkill there shows a badly negative bar for up to a second. maxLife is data as well, so a zero row divided by zero. Fixed with clamp(life/maxLife, 0, 1) over a guarded denominator, the fill skipped when the bar has no measurable width, and a one-off MON life<0 line that names the monster and the ratio. LL-056.

Checked the whole chain before changing anything, because a swap has only two homes: the art agrees with itself (spr_tusk_portrait is the boar and so is spr_tusk_walk; spr_zero_portrait is the blue hood and so is spr_zero_walk, and the colour sample of each portrait confirms which file is which) and so does scr_setupSpawning, so nothing on disk is swapped. What WAS broken: show_message_box APPENDS to a live box while the portrait is stored per MESSAGE and Draw_64 reads message_portrait[message_current], so a second preview could leave the box showing the previous creature with the previous portrait. A preview now destroys any live box and writes its portrait to every message; scr_makeMonster defaults every slot the enum names (debree 0, portrait -1); the boss bank prints walk and portrait names once at setup; up next logs the portrait by name; and test_content.py pins the portrait column as a bijection (6 tests), so a duplicate or a missing portrait now fails the suite. LL-057. If the bank line pairs Tusk-A-Lot with the hood, the two rows are simply named the other way round and the fix is two strings - that is rayu design call, not mine.

Rebuilt the Up Next path so the popup cannot name another creature. The pick is now ONE struct (wave, is_boss, index, name, portrait) made by scr_level_pick_store, which is idempotent per wave number - a second ask for the same wave returns the first answer instead of re-rolling, which is the only thing that made a mismatch possible. The portrait moved from a per-message array to one field for the whole box, so Draw_64 needs no index; the popup RESETS the live box instead of appending to it or destroying and re-creating it in one step; and SPAWN now compares the promise with the delivery and prints LEVEL WARNING when the wave, the row, the bank or the controller count disagree. LL-058, and four source-level tests in test_content.py pin the invariants (no irandom in SPAWN, idempotent pick, reset not append, portrait not indexed).

The reported symptom had a datum in it: it started on the THIRD level. stage_data gives 1-1 and 1-2 a one-creature pool and 1-3 the first two-creature pool, so a defect present since wave 1 of stage 1 could not be seen until then - and a one-message box is the only case where the old per-message portrait index could agree with itself. That is now a rule in LL-058: a symptom that starts on a particular stage is a data precondition, so look for what that stage changed.

Depth is now one rule for every actor: scr_depth_y(y) = -60 - y/32, derived from the world y of the feet, on the band the plants already occupied. Monsters re-derive it every step in obj_mon/Step_0, so a zombie walking behind a daisy is occluded by it and two crossing zombies keep a stable order; plants and the six gravestones derive it once at creation. Before this, monsters were a flat -60 written in three places, plants were always in front of every monster, and all six gravestones shared one depth (LL-059). A DEPTH line at level boot prints the band.

Every stage now authors an ordered [mid, end] boss pair and nothing is rolled: the mid boss arrives on boss_wave (waves div 2, derived in GameLevelData) and the end boss on the last wave. GardenToonASCII.ttf was never an install problem: it installed, it rendered blank. Every glyph was 90-215 separate 1-pixel-tall rectangle contours (20163 total) and the hinter snapped each one to zero height, so Qt drew 0 dark pixels at 13px. Rebuilt each glyph as one unioned outline (20163 -> 252 contours, 450KB -> 83KB, same em, advances and bboxes) and fixed the metadata that called a Regular font Bold (OS/2 usWeightClass 700, fsSelection 0x20, head.macStyle 1), the hmtx lsb of 0 against xMin 24-87, and OS/2 v0. Qt now draws 1355 dark pixels at 13px and 14958 at 48px. Tooling, backup and proof sheets: ~/Documents/GardenToonASCII-repair/.

Garden Toon was invisible to GameMaker for two reasons, not one. The Linux IDE discovers fonts by walking /usr/share/fonts and links no fontconfig, so a font installed for the user (fc-list and KDE both fine) does not exist for it; and the font itself is a COLR colour font whose white inset the IDE bakes with a 2015 FreeType, so it would have come out as solid black blobs at size 32/48. Rebound fnt_size12/16/20/32/48 to a COLR-free variant (GardenToonASCII-outline.ttf, the inset punched out of all 94 glyphs), sizes unchanged because the line heights match while strings grow 34-58% wider. Glyphs on disk stay Ink Free until rayu installs both TTFs into /usr/share/fonts and presses Regenerate Font Texture in each font. New lesson LL-066; roundtrip 0 differ, 170 tests OK.
Every UI draw_set_font now names a toon macro (34 sites, 14 files); the space borrows the backtick's slot so words are not em-spaced; ToonFontTests guards one-character-per-frame.

The GUI was pinned to 960x540 while the window was sized from the display aspect, so on anything but 16:9 the GUI and the camera view disagreed about their shape - and points_to_gui(), which divides one by the other, maps the pointer to the wrong place (11% off on a 16:10 monitor, which reads as 'the buttons are broken'). New scr_ui_screen owns the one decision: fixed design height 540, width = 540 * aspect, surface and port = the window, and the camera keeps its height and widens to the same aspect, so extra width is extra WORLD. New scr_ui_flex wraps the runtime's flexpanel API (trees are manual memory, rects are cached by node name and read with `false` so they are absolute), scr_ui_layout_menu describes the title/Options screen as a tree, and obj_ui (persistent) polls the window instead of trusting the Window Resize event. The menu's numbers are unchanged at 960x540: ui_menu_check() logs every one against the old hand-placed value with a 2px tolerance. Two static tests: every flexpanel symbol exists in the active runtime's fnames, and every ui_rect()/ui_place() name is a node in the layout. roundtrip 0 differ, 178 tests OK.

Fullscreen is a saved option now: scr_saveOptions writes slot [4] (0/1, read back from the window, not from a flag) and scr_loadOptions reads it behind `array_length(_data) > 4`, because the save is positional and a four-entry file would make _data[4] a fatal out-of-range read. The Options screen grows a second menu_options entry - a 'Fullscreen: Off/On' button whose label IS the state - and F11 does the same thing through obj_ui. Also fixed a toolkit bug found while filing these cards: _coerce() turned `awaiting=none` into null, so no backlog card could be created from the command line. True fullscreen is the default; a borderless window is the fallback if this machine picks a bad display mode.

Every monster was a 32x32 still (spr_mon) for its whole life because EVERY rig slot was built as -1: mon_rig_pick opened with if(!is_real(_slot)) return -1; and _slot is a ZOMB_ANIM value - enum values are stored as int64s and is_real answers FALSE for them (the manual is_real note; LL-034's landmine struck again). The user's own ~/GameMakerStudio2/debug.log had held the diagnosis all along - RIG walker N slots=4 walk=none for all fifteen creatures, was=spr_mon now=spr_mon on every corpse - while roundtrip, the 334-test suite and gml-functions were all green, because every gate reads GML as text and nobody read the run; the card's own 'what would prove it wrong: die=none' had fired unread. The is_real line is deleted (the bounds checks are the real guards), which unblocks the roster, dress-at-birth, the heal, the emerge switch and the fall in one line. LL-083 written; 2 new tests.

Second instance of the LL-083 landmine, found by sweeping every is_real in the project after the roster fix: menu_blur_wanted opened with if(!is_real(_state)) return false; and its caller (Menu/Draw_64.gml) passes menu_state - a MENU_STATE enum, stored as an int64 - so the guard answered FALSE for every state, no screen ever asked for the blur, and every meta screen sat over a SHARP backdrop with no line to say so (the not-wanted path prints nothing). The guard now asks for the -1 first-frame sentinel by name and lets the switch answer the rest; 1 new test pins it.

The rigs were authored at a larger, per-entity-varying pixel scale than the sheets they replace (appendage canvases up to 300px against whole walk sheets of 98-161px), so the creatures came out inconsistent. zomb_scml_scale_fix measures each entity once: a scratch player poses the walk clip at 8 samples, the union of drawn part rects (public get_part_world) gives the native footprint, and the fix brings its height to the original walk-sheet ART bbox height. Stamped by mon_rig_from, applied draw-time only in zomb_scml_draw, clamped 0.05-5, width ratio logged but never applied. 2 new tests, 355 -> 358 expected.
